name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Trahan with $1.8M cash on hand
model.rationale: Trahan is a well-funded incumbent in a D+11 district, while her Republican opponent has raised almost nothing. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Trahan is the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Lori Trahan seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about eleven points. She enters the general election with roughly $1.8 million on hand after raising over $1.6 million, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised about $7,000 and shows no outside support. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and her renomination status. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the usual possibility of low-turnout surprises in a race receiving little attention.
